tagline: Into Bluffton, where the old churches kept their walls.
intro: The May River route follows SC 46 about eight miles from the Jasper County line into Bluffton, then turns onto Boundary Street. The old town stands on the northern bluff of the river. Two thirds of it burned in 1863, and rebuilding came slowly.

Boundary Street’s Campbell Chapel passed from a white congregation to an African Methodist Episcopal congregation after the war. On nearby Calhoun Street, the Church of the Cross kept its Gothic building, with rose-colored glass brought from England.

moments.title: Campbell Chapel
moments.text: At 23 Boundary Street, the church acquired by an African Methodist Episcopal congregation in 1874 retains much of its nineteenth-century form and fabric.

moments.title: Church of the Cross
moments.text: On Calhoun Street, palmetto-like arches top the windows of a Gothic church built with rose-colored glass from England.
